To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we identified the genetic architecture of a mito-nuclear epistatic interaction that reduces the fitness of hybrids; (2) we found evidence that the X chromosomes are more likely to participate in mito-nuclear interactions than autosomes; and (3) we found evidence of linkage disequilibrium between the mitochondrial and X chromosomes in our population of recombinant lines.

the genetic architecture of a mito-nuclear incompatibility is consistent with the X chromosome participating in an epistatic interaction with both autosomes and the mitochondria, and that the accumulation of such mito-nuclear interactions could be the first step in the process of generating a new species.

we identified the genetic architecture of an intra-species mito-nuclear incompatibility and showed that the accumulation of such incompatibilities might contribute to the generation of inter-population hybrids with reduced fitness.
